articles.headline: Florida's Todd Golden: NCAA eligibility chaos self-inflicted
articles.description: Florida coach Todd Golden says the chaos of college eligibility is caused by the NCAA.

images.name: Alex Condon, Todd Golden [600x400]
images.caption: Alex Condon's decision to return to Florida boosts the outlook for Todd Golden's team in 2025-26.

articles.headline: SEC in filing: LSU dispute remains 'live,' school lacks institutional control
articles.description: The SEC is opposing LSU's request to dismiss the conference's lawsuit against the university and its officials, saying a live controversy still exists between the parties.

articles.headline: Best (and worst) men's college basketball offseason moves
articles.description: The best player and coach movement -- or lack thereof -- decisions this summer. Plus: The NCAA.

images.name: Matas Vokietaitis, Sean Miller [1296x729]
images.caption: Texas had the best overall 2026-27 offseason due to Sean Miller bringing back center Matas Vokietaitis and adding a strong mix of transfers and recruits around him.

images.name: Rick Barnes reveals portal strategy that built loaded Tennessee squad
images.caption: Terrence Hill Jr. and DeWayne Brown II join the desk at SEC Tipoff '27 to discuss how they are growing their games while Barnes discusses how he has built a talented team.

articles.headline: Jalen Smith, fixer in NCAA hoops betting scheme, sentenced to 6 years in prison
articles.description: Jalen Smith, 30, was charged with rigging college basketball games as part of a point-fixing scheme and sentenced to six years in federal prison.

images.name: NCAA Basketball (generic, 3/21/2015) [600x400] - Copy
images.caption: Thursday, March 17 will get the ball rolling for the first round of this year's men's NCAA tournament.

articles.headline: Ohio Gov. Mike DeWine signs order letting state's 2022 athletes play in 2026-27
articles.description: Ohio Gov. Mike DeWine signed an executive order allowing 2022 athletes to play even though the NCAA's new guidance excludes those who have already played four seasons.

articles.headline: Penny Hardaway offers to repay $2.6M loan for Memphis roster
articles.description: Memphis men's basketball coach Penny Hardaway says he's willing to pay up to $2.6 million this year toward the program's revenue-sharing total to field a competitive team.

images.name: Penny Hardaway [1296x729]
images.caption: Penny Hardaway is in the midst of his best campaign in seven seasons as the head coach at Memphis.
